q.t: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to:
q.e: A diagonal divides it into two triangles.

q.t: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are:
q.e: A diagonal makes two congruent triangles (ASA).

q.t: The diagonals of a parallelogram:
q.e: The triangles formed at the crossing point are congruent in pairs.

q.t: The diagonals of a rectangle are:
q.e: Each is the hypotenuse of a right triangle on the same two sides.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at:
q.e: All sides are equal, so each diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other.

q.t: A parallelogram with all sides equal and all angles 90° is a:
q.e: It is both a rhombus and a rectangle.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 80°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: Opposite angles are equal.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 80°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: Adjacent angles are supplementary.

q.t: The line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is:
o: Parallel to the third side and half of it
q.e: This is the midpoint theorem.

q.t: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 70°, 90° and 110°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 6. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 15 parts of 24°.

q.t: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are (3x − 20)° and (x + 40)°. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
In △ABC, D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC. BC = 12 cm. Find DE (in cm).
q.e: Midpoint theorem: DE = ½ BC.

q.t: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. Find its side (in cm).
q.e: Half-diagonals 8 and 6 at right angles.

q.t: A rectangle has diagonal 13 cm and one side 5 cm. Find the other side (in cm).
A parallelogram has perimeter 50 cm and adjacent sides in the ratio 3 : 2. Find the longer side (in cm).
q.e: Adjacent sides total 25 cm.

q.t: The quadrilateral formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of ANY quadrilateral is a:
q.e: Each pair of opposite sides is parallel to (and half of) the same diagonal.

q.t: The bisectors of the angles of a parallelogram enclose a:
q.e: Bisectors of adjacent (supplementary) angles meet at 90°.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A : ∠B = 2 : 7. Find ∠A (in degrees).
A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a:
q.e: The triangles at the crossing are congruent (SAS), giving equal alternate angles and so parallel sides.

q.t: The midpoints of the sides of a rectangle are joined in order. The figure formed is a:
q.e: Each new side is half a diagonal, and a rectangle’s diagonals are equal — so all four sides are equal.

q.t: The midpoints of the sides of a rhombus are joined in order. The figure formed is a:
q.e: The new sides are parallel to the diagonals, which are perpendicular — so the angles are 90°.

q.t: A triangle has perimeter 30 cm. Find the perimeter of the triangle formed by joining the midpoints of its sides (in cm).
q.e: Each new side is half of a side of the original.

q.t: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 10 cm and 16 cm. Find the length of the segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides (in cm).
q.e: It is the average of the parallel sides.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC bisects ∠A. Then ABCD is a:
q.e: ∠BAC = ∠DAC = ∠BCA (alternate), so AB = BC. Adjacent sides equal makes a rhombus.

q.t: In rhombus ABCD, ∠ABC = 70°. Find ∠ACB (in degrees).
q.e: BA = BC, so △ABC is isosceles: (180 − 70) ÷ 2.

q.t: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O and ∠AOD = 120°. Find ∠OAB (in degrees).
q.e: ∠AOB = 60° and OA = OB, so △OAB has base angles (180 − 60) ÷ 2 = 60°.

q.t: △ABC is right-angled at B and D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AC = 10 cm. Find BD (in cm).
q.e: The midpoint of the hypotenuse is equally far from all three vertices.

q.t: A triangle has area 48 cm². Find the area of the triangle formed by joining the midpoints of its sides (in cm²).
q.e: The midpoints divide it into 4 congruent triangles.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 10 cm and AD = 6 cm. The bisector of ∠A meets DC at E. Find EC (in cm).
q.e: ∠DEA = ∠EAB (alternate) = ∠DAE, so DE = AD = 6. EC = 10 − 6.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, E and F are the midpoints of AB and CD. Then AECF is a:
q.e: AE and CF are equal (half of equal sides) and parallel — one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is enough.

q.t: D, E, F are the midpoints of the sides of △ABC and △DEF has perimeter 18 cm. Find the perimeter of △ABC (in cm).
q.e: Each side of △ABC is twice the matching side of △DEF.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC, AB = 14 cm and DC = 8 cm. E is the midpoint of AD and EF ∥ AB meets BC at F. Find EF (in cm).
q.e: F is the midpoint of BC, and EF is the average of the parallel sides.

q.t: ABCD is a square and ABE is an equilateral triangle drawn INSIDE it. Find ∠DEC (in degrees).
q.e: AE = AD and ∠DAE = 30°, so ∠ADE = 75° and ∠EDC = 15°. Likewise ∠ECD = 15°. ∠DEC = 150°.

q.t: A diagonal of a rectangle makes 25° with one side. Find the acute angle between the diagonals (in degrees).
q.e: The half-diagonals are equal, forming an isosceles triangle with base angles 25°. Its exterior angle at the crossing is 50°.

q.t: The midpoints of the sides of a kite are joined in order. The figure formed is a:
q.e: The new sides are parallel to the kite’s diagonals, which are perpendicular.

q.t: A quadrilateral has diagonals that are equal and bisect each other. It must be a:
q.e: Bisecting makes it a parallelogram; equal diagonals make it a rectangle.

q.t: ABCD is a rhombus with ∠A = 60° and side 6 cm. Find the shorter diagonal (in cm).
q.e: △ABD has AB = AD and ∠A = 60°, so it is equilateral: BD = 6.

q.t: In △ABC, D is the midpoint of AB. A line through D parallel to BC meets AC at E. If AC = 9 cm, find AE (in cm).
q.e: Converse of the midpoint theorem: the line bisects the third side.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = (4x + 13)° and ∠D = (5x − 22)°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A and ∠D are adjacent: 9x − 9 = 180, x = 21. ∠D = 83°, and ∠B is opposite ∠D.
